thesis: Howard Marks argues that investors tend to trade too much, often selling appreciated assets simply to realize gains or avoid regret, and selling depressed assets due to psychological fear rather than sound reasoning. He concludes that it does not make sense to sell things just because they are up or just because they are down, suggesting that holding great winners and avoiding the tendency to increase positions as they rise or decrease them as they fall is preferable.
